figure.name: Robert Nozick
figure.role: Political philosopher focused on libertarian rights, entitlement theory, private property, and the minimal state.
figure.hook: Nozick = rights as limits on what society may do.
whyHere: Nozick belongs here because the capitalism/socialism road needs the rights-based argument against redistribution and broad state control.
He matters because property is not only an economic question. It is also an argument about rights, consent, coercion, and what government may legitimately take or require.
figure.cleanIdea: Nozick's path asks whether individual rights place hard limits on taxation, redistribution, and collective social goals.

figure.discussionText: This is the planned debate room for Nozick: rights, property, taxation, redistribution, consent, libertarianism, and the minimal state.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: A rights-based argument says redistribution and broad state power may violate individual entitlement and consent.

ideas.title: Libertarianism
ideas.plainDefinition: Libertarianism is a political philosophy that gives strong priority to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary exchange, and limits on state power.
ideas.context: In the Nozick path, libertarianism challenges redistributive policy by asking what government may take or command.
ideas.whyMatters: Libertarianism matters because the page must treat property-rights arguments seriously before comparing them with socialist and social-democratic claims.

ideas.title: Private Property
ideas.plainDefinition: Private property means property controlled by private owners rather than public bodies, common ownership, or direct state control.
ideas.context: In the Nozick path, private property is tied to individual rights and limits on redistribution.
ideas.whyMatters: Private property matters because capitalism, liberalism, socialism, and libertarianism disagree over what ownership permits and what society may require.

ideas.title: Minimal State
ideas.plainDefinition: A minimal state is a government limited mainly to protecting people against force, theft, fraud, and rights violations.
ideas.context: In the Nozick path, the minimal state is the boundary he argues government should not exceed.
ideas.whyMatters: Minimal state matters because it names the libertarian alternative to welfare-state and socialist policy claims.
